about: A sum of terabytes and gigabytes: dimensions agree, numbers do not.

files.model.yaml:
model: tiny
title: Mixed units
currency: USD

nodes:

  request_rate:
    kind: input
    decided: outside
    unit: request/second
    value: 200
    provenance: {kind: assumption, source: "the busy hour, as stated for this case"}

  service_demand:
    kind: input
    decided: outside
    unit: core*second/request
    value: 0.02
    provenance: {kind: assumption, source: "processor time per request, as stated for this case"}

  cores:
    kind: input
    decided: you
    unit: core
    value: 16
    provenance: {kind: assumption, source: "the fleet chosen for this case"}

  busy_cores:
    kind: derived
    unit: core
    formula: request_rate * service_demand

  utilisation:
    kind: derived
    unit: dimensionless
    formula: busy_cores / cores

  stored:
    kind: input
    decided: outside
    unit: TB
    value: 15
    provenance: {kind: assumption, source: "what is held, as stated for this case"}

  index:
    kind: input
    decided: outside
    unit: GB
    value: 500
    provenance: {kind: assumption, source: "the index, as stated for this case"}

  disk_per_host:
    kind: input
    decided: outside
    unit: TB/host
    value: 2
    provenance: {kind: assumption, source: "the disk each host has, as stated for this case"}

  total_stored:
    kind: derived
    unit: TB
    formula: stored + index

outputs:
  - utilisation
  - total_stored
files.scenarios/reference.yaml:
scenario: reference
title: Reference
because: the model as declared
samples: 1000
seed: 20260916
overrides: {}

point_error.message:
tiny does not typecheck, so it cannot be evaluated:
  - tiny: node 'total_stored' adds quantities in 'terabyte' and 'gigabyte': `stored + index`. The build converts a formula's result once, into the node's unit, so quantities that meet in a sum, a difference or a comparison must be declared in one unit. Declare them in one, or convert one of them in a node of its own.
